questions.question:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.

(A) a lot

(B) my daily routine

(C) i have missed

(D) since my retirement

(E) at the workplace
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Option (1)** i.e. **CBEAD**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **(C)** "I have missed" is the starting part because "I" is the subject and "have missed" is the verb phrase. It tells us what action is happening, which is the missing of something.
 
• **(B) **"my daily routine" comes after (C) because it tells us what the speaker has missed. Without this part, the sentence would be incomplete.
 
• **(E)** "at the workplace" specifies the location where the routine was carried out. This fits logically right after "my daily routine" to clarify the context.
 
• **(A)** "a lot" tells us how much the speaker misses their routine. This phrase is best placed after "I have missed" and before the time frame. It emphasizes the extent of what is being missed.
 
• **(D)** "since my retirement" gives us the time frame or the starting point of when the missing began.

 
 
• **Final Sentence:** "I have missed my daily routine at the workplace a lot since my retirement."

Therefore, the correct answer is **CBEAD****.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2 (**BACED**):** The phrase "a lot" is placed too early, disrupting the logical flow and making the sentence sound unnatural.
 
• **Option 3 (**BEADC**):** The phrase "since my retirement" is misplaced, disrupting the natural flow of the sentence.
 
• **Option 4 (**BADEC**):** "a lot" is incorrectly placed before "my daily routine" and "since my retirement" is out of place.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the following sentence in active voice.

The concert tickets were bought by my friend

options.text: My friend has bought the concert tickets.
My friend bought the concert tickets.
My friend buys the concert tickets.
My friend is buying the concert tickets.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In active voice, the subject performs the action expressed by the verb. The original sentence in passive voice is: "The concert tickets were bought by my friend." Here, the subject (concert tickets) receives the action.
 
• To convert this into active voice, the object "concert tickets" becomes the direct object in the active sentence.
 
• In active voice, the correct sentence would be: "My friend bought the concert tickets."
 
• The correct verb form to use here is the past tense "bought," which reflects the action completed in the past.
 
• Therefore, the correct transformation of the sentence into active voice is "My friend bought the concert tickets."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"My friend bought the concert tickets."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **"My friend has bought the concert tickets." – This is in the present perfect tense, which is incorrect for the context, as the original sentence refers to a simple past action.
 
• **Option 3: **"My friend buys the concert tickets." – This is in the simple present tense, which implies a habitual action, not a specific past event.
 
• **Option 4: **"My friend is buying the concert tickets." – This is in the present continuous tense, which refers to an action happening right now, not in the past.

questions.solution:

• Following the introduction, "it is written that Brahma is the God of creation" **(DB)** continues the logical sequence, making it clear what is written in the book.
 
• **The next part,** "and it is He who has made," starts the explanation about what Brahma has done, indicated by (C).
 
• **Ending with **"all the plants and animals of today" (A) completes the sentence by stating what Brahma has created.

Therefore, the correct answer is **DBCA.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Option 3 (DCBA):** This option starts with "in the book of Hindu mythology all the plants and animals of today," which makes the sentence incorrect as it disrupts the logical flow.
 
• **Option 4 (CABD):** This option starts with "all the plants and animals of today and it is He who has made," which creates a fragmented and confusing sentence structure.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

Inayat did not greet her.

options.text: She was not going to be greeted by Inayat.
She was not at all greeted by Inayat.
She was not greeted by Inayat.
She was not being greeted by Inayat.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "Inayat did not greet her."
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "her" at the beginning.
 
• Change the active verb form "did not greet" to "was not greeted" (simple past passive).
 
• Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "Inayat."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"She was not greeted by Inayat."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **"She was not going to be greeted by Inayat." – Incorrect tense and structure.
 
• **Option 2: **"She was not at all greeted by Inayat." – Adds unnecessary emphasis, changing the meaning slightly.
 
• **Option 4: **"She was not being greeted by Inayat." – Incorrect continuous tense.
